repo.description:
### Summary

NocoDB enabled Express's proxy trust unconditionally at startup, so the client address of every request was taken from caller-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` headers even when no trusted proxy sat in front of the instance. Any caller, including an anonymous public-form submitter, could choose the source IP address recorded in the audit log.

### Details

The server entry files (`run/local.ts`, `run/docker.ts` and their Enterprise counterparts) called `server.enable('trust proxy')` with no way to turn it off, so Express derived `req.ip`, which audit records store, from the forwarding headers of each request. Other consumers, among them telemetry, exception logs and the public API rate limiter, read the address through the `request-ip` middleware, which parses the same headers on its own. The fix, in `Noco.ts` and `utils/trustProxy.ts`, turns proxy trust off by default and enables it only for the topology an operator sets in `NC_TRUST_PROXY`, and every consumer now reads the trust-aware `req.ip`.

### Impact

No authentication is required. On an instance reachable directly, or through a proxy that passes client-supplied forwarding headers on, a caller could write an arbitrary source IP address into the audit log and other request logs, misleading investigation and attribution, and could evade the per-address limit of the public API rate limiter. No authentication bypass or IP-based access-control bypass is involved. After the fix, setting `NC_TRUST_PROXY=true` without a proxy that overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` restores the earlier behaviour, by design.

### Credit

This issue was reported by [@5255fgh](https://github.com/5255fgh) (白墨).
repo.summary: IP Address Spoofing via Unconditional Proxy Trust
